record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: Find an algebraic characterization of colored graphs whose associated colored-graph polyhedron is PL homeomorphic to the standard n-sphere S^n for n >= 3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A colored graph (also called a gem or crystallization in the sense of graph-encoded manifolds) is a pair (G, γ), where G is a finite multigraph that is regular of degree n+1, and γ : E(G) → {0, 1, …, n} is an edge coloring such that the edges meeting at every vertex receive pairwise distinct colors. Associated to (G, γ) is a pseudocomplex K(G, γ), constructed by taking, for each vertex of G, an abstract n-simplex with vertices labeled 0, 1, …, n, and identifying the (n−1)-face opposite to the vertex labeled i in two simplices whenever the corresponding two vertices of G are joined by an edge of color i (the identification preserving vertex labels). The polyhedron |K(G, γ)| is the geometric realization of this pseudocomplex.

Problem. For each integer n ≥ 3, give an algebraic characterization (in terms of the combinatorial/algebraic invariants of the coloring, such as the structure of the subgraphs induced by subsets of colors, their connected components, and associated chain or group-theoretic data) of those colored graphs (G, γ) of degree n+1 for which |K(G, γ)| is PL homeomorphic to the standard n-sphere S^n.
artifact.status_search_result: Recognition of the n-sphere is known to be undecidable for n ≥ 5 and unresolved algorithmically in lower dimensions in general, and no algebraic characterization of crystallizations of S^n for n ≥ 3 appears in the literature. The problem is generally treated as open, with only heuristic and partial recognition results available.

status_evidence.title: Heuristics for Sphere Recognition
status_evidence.snippet: The problem of determining whether a given simplicial complex is homeomorphic to a sphere is undecidable, though practical heuristics exist.
status_evidence.claim: No general algorithmic/algebraic characterization is known; sphere recognition is undecidable in high dimensions, supporting the problem being open.

status_evidence.title: Graph-encoded 3-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Crystallizations and graph-encoded manifolds provide a graph-theoretic framework for PL-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework of the problem but no algebraic sphere characterization.
